brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Full bases piece:0,0,0 and piece:-1,1,0 plus the half base piece:0,1,0 (half-n), with open faces capped and joints bolted (jointBolt x3).

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) and bin:-1,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) are drop-in trays that hang on their own rim with no fixings, so they lift out. They hold the screw, nut and standoff props. The top covers sit over them, so a cover has to come off before a bin can be lifted out.
drawer:0#0,1#cut is in the cut face of the half base at 0,1, with a solder reel inside.

handle:0,0,0;top is placed with its three inserts, across the corner where the top covers of all three cells meet. It fits, but the configurator checks fit only, so I can't confirm it is strong enough to carry the loaded organizer.

It is three cells, about the footprint of two and a half hex bases, with a top handle. Whether it is light and strong enough to carry depends on the print material, which the configurator does not check.

finish.summary: I built a compact three-cell organizer with removable bins, one drawer and a carry handle. There are two full hex bases, each holding a drop-in bin with compartments, and a north half base with a drawer in its cut face. Top covers close all three cells. The handle sits across the corner where the three covers meet, because the configurator only accepts a handle there. Open faces are capped and the joints bolted. check_build passes with no rule issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear. For staging, I put M3 screws, nuts and standoffs in the bin compartments, a solder reel in the drawer and electrical tape on the half cover. One more prop wouldn't fit in a bin compartment. The props in the bins can't be seen while the covers are on. I didn't check how strong the handle is or whether it can carry a loaded organizer; the configurator only checks fit.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
